body: In the form's reset(), I see that it removes everything of the form, including the refs. Why need to do that, I thought reset() is only for reseting the values and errors only?
thanks @durianjc  i am looking at it now

Btw, my use case is doing dynamic fields in the form, for example of a filter form where user can add/remove inputs (more/less filters) in the form. I can see that it may have problems with input refs, especially when removing an input. Could it be able to export an "unregister()" function to remove and clean up an input (field) in form? What do you think?

hey @durianjc,

this is the problem with reset()

```
<button type="button" onClick={() => reset()}>
  reset
</button>
```

your button didn't have a type, so browser treat it as 'submit', so it's a `submit` with `reset`.
when your input gets removed, it should auto unregister :)
